Frosted Pumpkin Cookies

ByKelsey Byrnes
0 Comments
Published onOctober 8, 2026
Jump to Recipe

Instaread

These soft Frosted Pumpkin Cookies are incredibly tender and adorned with a layer of cream cheese frosting on top. The addition of pudding mix keeps them moist and bakery-soft for days, so the last cookie is just as good as the first!

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

These pumpkin cookies remind me of my favorite fall dessert (my frosted pumpkin bars) but in cookie form! The pudding mix is my secret for keeping them soft and moist for days, but also sturdy enough to handle the dreamy layer of frosting! They’re simple to make so you can have a yummy fall treat on the table before you know it!

Ingredients Needed

The full list of ingredients and amounts are in the recipe card below, but I wanted to draw attention to a few of them along with some substitutions:

  • Pudding Mix – I love the combination of the butterscotch flavor with the pumpkin. It’s very subtle but it really helps keep the cookie moist. Use instant pudding mix; though pumpkin spice or vanilla pudding mix will work, too.
  • Pumpkin Pie Spice – You can use store-bought or make your own with cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and allspice!
  • Pumpkin Puree – Make sure to use pumpkin puree and not pumpkin pie mix.
  • Cream Cheese – You’ll want to use block cream cheese for this (vs the tubs of spreadable cream cheese) so the texture is thick and creamy.

Recipe Testing to Find the BEST!

Recipe testing is one of my favorite parts of my job. I get to think back to my food science courses where I learned all about ingredients and how they interact. Here’s what I tried…

Save This Recipe For Later

Get the recipe emailed to you + sign up for all our latest!

  • Butter vs Oil – The flavor of butter is always better than oil (in my opinion) but in this case, the pumpkin flavor is really the star! The texture of the cookies with the oil was more tender than with the butter.
  • Number of Eggs – I wanted soft cookies, but not so soft that they wouldn’t hold their shape with frosting. I thought an extra egg might help hold up the structure, but the water from the egg white seemed to add too much moisture.
  • Adding Pudding Mix – The addition of pudding mix was an idea I had after adding butterscotch pudding to my pumpkin cupcakes. The pudding adds great structure to the cookies and keeps them so soft!

How to Make Soft Pumpkin Cookies with Cream Cheese Frosting

Start by combining the dry ingredients in a bowl. They’ll get added into the dough later, but I like having them mixed first so the pudding can be well-dispersed.

To start the dough, add the wet ingredients (and the sugar) to a mixing bowl. I like to use a whisk or an electric mixer to make sure it’s well-combined.

Then stir in the dry ingredients. It’ll look more like a thick batter than a classic cookie dough. Be sure to scrape down the sides of the bowl to ensure everything gets well-incorporated.

Scoop the dough onto parchment-lined baking sheets, making sure to give them a little room to spread as they bake. Bake the cookies one pan at a time so they cook evenly.

Once they come out of the oven, let them cool for a couple minutes before removing to a wire rack.

Once the cookies are completely cooled, it’s time to frost them (or else the frosting will melt and run right off the cookies!).

To make the frosting, you’ll start by combining the softened butter and cream cheese. Then add the powdered sugar and stir until smooth. If it feels too thick, you can add a little bit of milk, but be sure you have the powdered sugar incorporated before you do so (cream cheese has enough moisture that you really shouldn’t need milk).

Storage Instructions

In the Fridge: These cookies can be stored in the fridge for up to 5 days. I recommend storing these in a single layer so they don’t stick together. If you must stack them, add a sheet of waxed paper or parchment between layers.

In the Freezer: Store in the freezer (frosted or unfrosted) for up to 2 months.

Recipe Variations

  • Skip the frosting and add 1 cup of mini chocolate chips to the batter.
  • Make browned butter cream cheese frosting for even more flavor.
  • Make them gluten-free! Most pudding mixes are free of gluten (though of course you’ll want to double-check all ingredient labels, of course), so all you should have to do is swap the flour out for a gluten free flour.

Frosted Pumpkin Cookies

Author: Kelsey Byrnes
30 large cookies
These soft Frosted Pumpkin Cookies are incredibly tender and adorned with a layer of cream cheese frosting on top. The addition of pudding mix keeps them moist and bakery-soft for days, so the last cookie is just as good as the first!
Print
Pin
Rate
Save Saved!

Equipment

  • Cookie Sheets

Ingredients
 

Soft Pumpkin Cookies

  • 2 cups flour
  • 1 3.4-ounce packet instant butterscotch pudding mix
  • 1 tablespoon pumpkin pie spice
  • 2 teaspoons baking soda
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup vegetable oil
  • 1 cup sugar
  • 1 15-ounce can pumpkin puree
  • 3 eggs
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract

Cream Cheese Frosting

  • 6 ounces cream cheese softened
  • 2 tablespoons butter softened
  • 2 cups powdered sugar

Instructions

Make the Cookies

  • Preheat the oven to 350℉ and line a couple cookie sheets with parchment paper or silicone baking mats.
  • In a mixing bowl, combine the dry ingredients; set aside.
    2 cups flour, 1 3.4-ounce packet instant butterscotch pudding mix, 1 tablespoon pumpkin pie spice, 2 teaspoons baking soda, 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • In a separate large mixing bowl, whisk together the vegetable oil, sugar, pumpkin, eggs, and vanilla extract.
    1 cup vegetable oil, 1 cup sugar, 1 15-ounce can pumpkin puree, 3 eggs, 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  • Add the dry ingredients and stir until smooth.
  • Use a cookie scoop (I used a #24 cookie scoop; just under 3 tablespoons) to form cookies on the prepared baking sheet, leaving at least 2 inches between cookies.
  • Bake one pan at a time for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown around the edges and set on top.
  • Let cool for 2-3 minutes and transfer to a cooling rack to cool completely.

Frost the Cookies

    Be sure that the cream cheese and the butter are both softened before making the frosting to ensure a smooth (vs lumpy) frosting.
  • Beat the cream cheese and butter together.
    6 ounces cream cheese, 2 tablespoons butter
  • Add the powdered sugar and mix until smooth.
    2 cups powdered sugar
  • Spread onto cooled cookies and enjoy!

Notes

I really love these cookies with butterscotch pudding mix as the flavor pairs so well with the pumpkin spice!  If you can’t find butterscotch, you can use vanilla in its place.
